learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparison of numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Committed 30% for guilt in the case where my vote matters. Prompt specified three jurors, 70% reliable clues, equal prior and unanimity.
observations.exploration: Initial all-innocent clues gave 7%. Flipping Juror 1 gave 30% with no pivotal vote; flipping Juror 2 gave 70% and pivotal Yes. Flipping my vote convicted without changing the bar; reversing it acquitted at the same 70%.
observations.reveal: Correction explained that other jurors vote their clues, so being pivotal supplies two guilty clues against one innocent clue. Distinguished evidence from the vote itself.
observations.visual: Actual dark 1257 by 936 screenshots inspected. Three figures separately label clues and votes; probability bar and verdict badges make the independence of my vote from evidence visible. Reveal is readable.
observations.previewIsolation: Preview banner said learning history and analytics are not saved.
observations.blinding: No source, metadata or other reviewer judgments read.

prediction.reason: Concrete probability commitment, but critical assumptions arrive after the prediction.
prediction.evidence: Others voting their clues is explained in reveal; conditional independence is not stated.

interaction.reason: Reversible switches separate evidence updates from a decisive action.
interaction.evidence: My vote changed verdict while probability stayed 70%.

payoff.reason: Reveal connects pivotality to information rather than mere power.
payoff.evidence: Two other guilty votes disclose two guilty clues in this setup.

clarity.reason: Diagram distinguishes clues from votes, but the probabilistic model is underspecified.
clarity.evidence: 70% reliability and equal prior alone do not establish independent signals; rational voting also needs loss assumptions.

transfer.reason: Reusable conditioning idea appears with no fresh scenario.
transfer.evidence: Only the original three-juror setup is exercised.

accessibility.evidence: Ordinary clicks and visual screenshots only.

surprise.reason: An innocent clue can coexist with 70% guilt in the pivotal case.

visualExplanation.reason: Separate clues, votes, bar and verdict show the key contrast.
visualExplanation.evidence: Vote toggle changes verdict but not probability.

practicalValue.reason: Illustrates conditional information, with consequential real-world framing needing caution.
practicalValue.evidence: No decision losses or real legal standards modeled.

depth.reason: Distinguishes sincere evidence from conditioning on influence.
depth.evidence: Pivotality reveals other signals under their voting rule.

complexity.reason: Conditional inference plus a unanimity decision rule requires tracking several assumptions.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Condition on the pivotal event and separate evidence from an action.
complexity.prerequisiteNovelty: Conditional probability and strategic voting are new.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: Percent probability and distinct clue/vote labels.

whyCool: The vote can move the verdict while leaving the evidence bar unchanged.
caveat: The exact posterior needs conditional independence; rational conviction also depends on decision losses. Those conditions are not stated in the visible walkthrough.
effort: Approximately 3 minutes of actual browser review.
